health_and_wellness.summary: Jacob maintains health through practical movement and beach-based activity, while managing work-related joint pain and low-level stress.

Manages knee ache, right-shoulder stiffness, lower-back strain, and a recent tendinitis flare-up from overhead painting with stretching, ice, ibuprofen, exercises, and smarter ladder/bucket use (Q31, Q33, Q34).
Uses ibuprofen, ice, stretching, and limited marijuana gummies for soreness or sleep, avoiding prescription pain pills because he has seen tradesmen get tangled up with pills (Q39).

Has delayed dental care and physical therapy because thin insurance, cash flow, and unpaid time off make care costly (Q36, Q40).

summaries.demographer: Jacob Bowden is a 58-year-old white non-Hispanic man born in Torrance, California and living alone in a rented one-bedroom back unit in Redondo Beach (Q84-Q90, Q51, Q58). He is divorced, not cohabiting, and has two adult children, Sarah and Daniel, plus a grandson, Mateo (Q05, Q84). His formal education ended after eighth grade, and he has spent more than thirty years in residential and light commercial painting work (Q01, Q65, Q76, Q90). His life-course profile is working-class, locally rooted, and shaped by high coastal housing costs, self-employment, and aging manual labor (Q08, Q31, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Jacob's choices reflect strong present-oriented work habits formed in adolescence, but he is now shifting toward longer-term investment through GED prep, licensing, and savings (Q02, Q18, Q61, Q108). He is risk-aware rather than risk-seeking: he can cover a $400 emergency but worries about injury, slow clients, truck repairs, and the fragility of self-employment (Q64, Q82, Q83). His spending priorities are rent, vehicle reliability, tools, health basics, and family, while discretionary cuts fall on eating out, travel, and tools that can wait (Q56-Q63). summaries.political_scientist: Jacob is an Independent who leans Democratic, with moderate, practical views rooted in labor, health care, housing affordability, environmental protection, and small-contractor concerns (Q23-Q25, Q95, Q96). He votes in presidential and most local elections but has missed primaries, indicating partial but meaningful civic participation (Q23). He expresses conditional institutional trust: he respects public health sources and practical regulation, but is skeptical of party promises and bureaucratic waste (Q24, Q42, Q95). On race and policing, he supports accountability and says Black Lives Matter affected him somewhat, mainly through listening to coworkers and family rather than protest participation (Q26-Q30).
summaries.psychologist: Jacob presents as pragmatic, conscientious, and identity-bound to competence, usefulness, and self-reliance (Q01, Q65, Q109). He regulates stress through routine, ocean activity, guitar, practical problem-solving, and selective disclosure to trusted people such as Pete and family (Q43-Q45, Q50). His emotional vulnerabilities center on money insecurity, loneliness, aging, and regret over leaving school early, but he channels them into concrete plans rather than abstract rumination (Q02, Q43, Q83, Q108). Relationally, he is loyal but not highly expressive, maintaining steady ties with adult children, his sister, friends, and community contacts through practical help and shared activities (Q05-Q07, Q17).
